name: DevContext graph-v2 — autonomous remainder

stages.title: R4 MCP correctness + honesty fixes (R4 §1 items 1-7)
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/R4-MCP-PROPER-TOOL.md §1 — items 1-7 are the whole specification, each with an [audit] file:line ref. RE-VERIFY every [audit] ref before editing (PLAN.md §5 rule 2): they were taken on 2026-07-27 and Batches A-E have moved code since. Most live in src/DevContext.Mcp/DevContextTools.cs. Evidence for a claim is a real MCP call showing the new response shape, not a diff.

stages.title: R4 menu hygiene + one trace default (items 11-12)
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/R4-MCP-PROPER-TOOL.md §1 items 11-12. Item 12 is now mostly done upstream: Batch E made TracePolicy the single seam order + budget rule (PLAN.md §2 S5), so this is aligning the MCP's 4000-token default to it, not inventing a policy. Item 11's trap is the SECOND hard-coded tool list behind the did-you-mean handler — it drifts from the real one; make it read the reflected list.

stages.title: R4 missing primitives: seam / kind-filtered neighbours / cache truth (8-10)
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/R4-MCP-PROPER-TOOL.md §1 items 8-10. These touch proto + GraphQuery, so a proto change means rebuilding DevContext.Contracts AND `pnpm gen:proto`, wiring server + app in lockstep. GraphQuery already supports kind-filtered neighbours — only proto/tools do not expose it (3 fields). seam(from,to) is the highest-value new primitive and exists at no layer today.

stages.title: R4 dogfood drive — is the MCP a proper tool?
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/R4-MCP-PROPER-TOOL.md §2 (protocol) and §3 (the success bar this is graded against). This stage RUNS the tool rather than editing it — the battery-collapse rule does not apply to driving the MCP, that IS the deliverable. Grade honestly: a HURT verdict is a finding, not a failure. Judge against §3's bar (>=8/10 answered without grep fallback). If the answer is 'it did not help', say so and say why — that is the useful result.

stages.title: D-3 — a CLI verb reaches its handler
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/DECISIONS.md (D-D, and the S8 surprise 3 that corrected the brief). This is real engine work. GitVersion's five verbs are ICommand<TSettings> classes whose execute member never joined. Note the precedent from Batch E's CleanArchitecture case: a shape-based fallback needs TWO structural facts and NO name list — do not pattern-match on names. ROOT-CAUSE PER VERB FROM THE RAW DUMPS BEFORE ANY CODE MOVES (that ordering is what made Batch E work).

stages.title: D-4 — one vocabulary for "service" on Atlas
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/DECISIONS.md, the D-F..D-H section (D-4 is the live find inside D-H). Three vocabularies on ONE page: the canvas excludes ClientApp/HybridApp, the per-service breakdown lists them AS services, and Hub radar mixes services with types. Separately, raw metadata arity is reaching the UI as Logging.ILogger`1 — that is a rendering leak, fix it wherever the arity survives. Pick ONE definition, state it, and make all three obey it.

stages.title: C-2 / C-3 — a library's empty sections fill or withhold with a reason
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/DECISIONS.md — D-C, plus the S9 scope correction that is the governing precedent: the Confidence Ledger was suppressed entirely on entry-less repos (every library), and the fix was to show the panel and have the two entry-dependent ROWS withhold themselves. That is C-3's rule; apply the same shape to Atlas's five empty sections. A section that withholds must say WHY it is empty.

stages.title: R1 scale wall — profile HotChocolate, do not raise the timeout
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/PLAN.md, the section 'Open R1 items S5 leaves on the table'. HotChocolate (ChilliCream/graphql-platform) produced no dump in 28 minutes and timed out at the 600s budget, while PowerToys (83s) and bitwarden-server (214s) finish — so this is ONE repo an order of magnitude past the rest, not a general regression. It needs a PROFILE, not a bigger timeout; use the devcontext-bench skill for per-phase timings. An accepted limitation with the class NAMED is a valid outcome; a raised timeout is not.

stages.title: R1 archetype loses to an auxiliary executable (CLI, MahApps.Metro)
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/PLAN.md, 'Open R1 items S5 leaves on the table'. ONE root cause, TWO poles: dotnet/command-line-api reads CliTool and MahApps.Metro reads Desktop, because a demo/sample executable that is not under a samples/ path outranks the packable library it demonstrates. Both are pinned RED with the truth declared — DO NOT re-declare the expectations to match the engine. Batch D's ArchetypeDetector is pure and reads ProjectInfo.Sdks, which is where evidence now lives.

stages.title: Sweep for thresholds calibrated on pre-Batch-A data
stages.notes: STRAND DOC: docs/dev/research/DECISIONS.md, the 'regression E-2 uncovered' note. The known case: START HERE's checkout special case was written when every checkout-titled entry was a 1-hop client command that could not clear a >=4-node gate; Batches A-E made that comment false and the special case began beating the preference it existed to protect. Find the OTHERS. A threshold whose justifying comment describes a starved graph is the signature. Re-measure each on current data; correct it or justify it in a comment that STATES the measurement (S9's habit, three-for-three the most valuable one in this program).

promptExtra:
TRAPS THIS PROGRAM HAS ALREADY PAID FOR — do not rediscover them:
1. A backtick inside an HTML comment TERMINATES an Angular template literal. This has fired three times. Worse, `pnpm ng build` piped through grep for error markers looks CLEAN because esbuild emits ANSI colour codes before the failure marker. CHECK $?, never the filtered output. Write field names in comments without backticks.
2. Every `node scripts/...` command needs an absolute `cd` in the SAME command — a drifted working directory has cost this program two sessions.
3. `analyze` takes a POSITIONAL path; `query` takes `--path`. `analyze --path <repo>` silently analyses the working directory instead.
4. Rebuild src/DevContext.Cli after ANY Core edit — the CLI carries its own DevContext.Core.dll (stale-dll trap).
5. CLI paths must be ABSOLUTE — a relative path is parsed as a GitHub repo and cloned.
6. Restart src/DevContext.App/scripts/start-dev-bg.ps1 before any Playwright capture that follows a build; a stale vite-error-overlay silently eats clicks.
7. MEASURE a verdict, do not read it off a doc comment. Three times in this program the doc comment was stale and the code was right. Checking what a field CONTAINS is the highest-value habit here.
8. Never weaken a measurement to get green: no deleted tests, no relaxed expectations, no softened gate. If a bar is genuinely wrong, put a HUMAN: line in the tracker handoff and stop.
9. Never merge to develop. That is an owner-signed event.
